prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py blindly calls json.loads() on any string-valued argument whose field annotation is not exactly `str`, which corrupts legitimate string values for union/optional-str parameters (e.g. a str|None field receiving the literal string "123" or "null" gets silently converted to int/None instead of staying a string). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py blindly calls json.loads() on any string-valued argument whose field annotation is not exactly `str`, which corrupts legitimate string values for union/optional-str parameters (e.g. a str|None field receiving the literal string "123" or "null" gets silently converted to int/None instead of staying a string). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a helper to gate pre-parsing based on the annotation shape, but they cover different edge cases and each misses a case the other catches. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` checks `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` (a frozenset of plain types) for each union member — this fails to recognize `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None`, the idiomatic pattern for a described optional string param, because an `Annotated[...]` object is never equal to the plain `str` type by set membership, so it falls through and still pre-parses (bug not fixed for that common case). #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` specifically to strip `Annotated` off each union member before checking, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` is correctly skipped. Conversely, #2032's `_SIMPLE_TYPES` set also skips pre-parsing for broader simple-type unions like `str | int` or `str | bool`, which #3056's narrower `_is_optional_str` (str-or-None only) does not cover. Recommend keeping #3056 since it correctly handles the more common Annotated/Field-described-optional-str pattern; the additional simple-type-union coverage from #2032 could be ported into #3056's helper if needed.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a helper to gate pre-parsing based on the annotation shape, but they cover different edge cases and each misses a case the other catches. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` checks `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` (a frozenset of plain types) for each union member — this fails to recognize `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None`, the idiomatic pattern for a described optional string param, because an `Annotated[...]` object is never equal to the plain `str` type by set membership, so it falls through and still pre-parses (bug not fixed for that common case). #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` specifically to strip `Annotated` off each union member before checking, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` is correctly skipped. Conversely, #2032's `_SIMPLE_TYPES` set also skips pre-parsing for broader simple-type unions like `str | int` or `str | bool`, which #3056's narrower `_is_optional_str` (str-or-None only) does not cover. Recommend keeping #3056 since it correctly handles the more common Annotated/Field-described-optional-str pattern; the additional simple-type-union coverage from #2032 could be ported into #3056's helper if needed.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a helper to gate pre-parsing based on the annotation shape, but they cover different edge cases and each misses a case the other catches. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` checks `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` (a frozenset of plain types) for each union member — this fails to recognize `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None`, the idiomatic pattern for a described optional string param, because an `Annotated[...]` object is never equal to the plain `str` type by set membership, so it falls through and still pre-parses (bug not fixed for that common case). #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` specifically to strip `Annotated` off each union member before checking, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` is correctly skipped. Conversely, #2032's `_SIMPLE_TYPES` set also skips pre-parsing for broader simple-type unions like `str | int` or `str | bool`, which #3056's narrower `_is_optional_str` (str-or-None only) does not cover. Recommend keeping #3056 since it correctly handles the more common Annotated/Field-described-optional-str pattern; the additional simple-type-union coverage from #2032 could be ported into #3056's helper if needed.

clusters.pick_reason: #3246 fixes the same root cause described in #2492 (broken token endpoint due to missing oauth_metadata after restart) by guarding the existing proactive-refresh branch with `oauth_metadata is not None`, requiring no API changes and working regardless of storage backend. #2492 instead adds two new methods (get_oauth_metadata/set_oauth_metadata) to the TokenStorage Protocol, which only fixes the endpoint problem for storage backends that implement them — the SDK-provided storages don't, so the broken fallback path #3246 addresses remains unfixed for them. #3246 also references the originating issue (#3240) directly.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add the same in-flight duplicate-id rejection, but #3063 keys the stream dict with str(message.id), which collapses the JSON-RPC-valid distinction between integer id 1 and string id "1" (a false 409 or cross-wire) and doesn't guard against a string id colliding with the internal GET_STREAM_KEY sentinel. #3221 introduces a type-preserving `_request_stream_key` (`i:`/`s:` prefixes) that fixes both edge cases while solving the same underlying problem, so it supersedes #3063's diff.
